title: Kepler Reach Rising Again
premise: Lior Crane, a xenolinguist stranded on the fading colony of Kepler Reach, discovers that the colony's founding manifest lists a ship — the Meridian — that never flew, carrying a passenger whose name matches her own dead mother's. The lie: two rival fleets hovering over the Reach each believe the other holds the codes to the colony's failing reactor, and Lior's recordings of the dying settlement are the only 'proof' keeping them from open war. As she traces her mother's forged identity through the Meridian's sealed logs, she realizes the reactor countdown was never an accident but an inheritance test left by the founders. In the end, Lior broadcasts her mother's voice — and her own confession — to both fleets, choosing truth over the sustaining lie; the fleets stand down, the reactor is saved by the code hidden in her childhood lullabies, and Lior finally dreams again in a language no one has ever spoken.
about_author: Emrys Delacroix is the pen name of a former deep-space telemetry analyst who spent six years listening to signals nobody answered. They write about people who keep records for a living and secrets for survival.

chapters.title: The Last Fluent Speaker
chapters.summary: Lior Crane records the emptying market district of Kepler Reach, cataloguing dialects dying with their speakers. Her POV establishes her loneliness and her strange new symptom: she now dreams in sounds she cannot transcribe. Emotional beat: quiet grief disguised as professional detachment.

chapters.title: A Ship That Never Flew
chapters.summary: While archiving colonial manifests, Lior finds the Meridian listed as departed with full crew — yet it still sits in the orbital graveyard. Among its passengers: Maren Crane, her mother, who died before Lior was born on-world. POV: Lior. Beat: the first crack in everything she believes about her origins.

chapters.title: Two Fleets at the Window
chapters.summary: Lior learns why no one talks about the sky: the Concord fleet and the Vessel Compact have orbited in stalemate for a decade, each convinced the other controls the reactor failsafes. The governor begs Lior to keep broadcasting her 'neutral' recordings that both sides read as reassurance. Beat: the weight of an accidental lie.

chapters.title: Maren Crane, Passenger
chapters.summary: Breaking into the Meridian's sealed hold, Lior finds her mother's cabin preserved — and evidence Maren boarded under a forged identity created by the founders themselves. POV shifts briefly to a Compact boarding officer, Ilsa Vey, who notices someone entered the graveyard dock. Beat: inheritance as mystery.

chapters.title: What the Reactor Remembers
chapters.summary: The reactor's countdown accelerates without cause. Lior discovers the founders embedded a linguistic key into its control chants — a language matching the one invading her dreams. Beat: dread turning to purpose; her affliction may be a message.

chapters.title: Ilsa Vey Interrogates a Ghost
chapters.summary: Ilsa detains Lior after tracing the dock breach, but instead of arrest, offers a bargain: help the Compact verify the reactor codes, or both fleets assume the worst. Lior realizes either side 'winning' means war. Beat: alliance built on mutual suspicion.

chapters.title: The Lullaby Cipher
chapters.summary: Decoding her mother's journals, Lior maps the founders' plan: the reactor crisis is a test, and the key is the lullaby Maren sang her — composed in the founders' engineered language. But singing it aloud will reveal to both fleets that the codes were never held by either. Beat: the lie begins to die.

chapters.title: Countdown and Countdown
chapters.summary: Concord detects the Compact's boarding activity; both fleets arm. The governor demands Lior broadcast calming recordings; instead she must choose between preserving the fragile lie and transmitting the truth. Ilsa, ordered to seize the cipher, hesitates. Beat: everything converges, trust fraying.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax. With the reactor minutes from failure, Lior seizes the colony's transmitter and sends her mother's lullaby plus her own confession — the lie, the forgery, the test — to both fleets in the founders' language, which every human ear half-remembers. The fleets freeze; the reactor accepts the song. Beat: raw exposure, then stunned silence across two bridges.

chapters.title: Rising Again
chapters.summary: Resolution. The fleets negotiate openly for the first time; colonists return to districts they'd abandoned. Lior, no longer keeper of a lie, teaches the recovered language to children — and finally dreams a whole sentence in it, understanding at last what her mother left her. Beat: belonging earned, identity chosen, inheritance accepted.
